purpose.summary: This subprogram (ORCSPTNUM) is part of the ORCA JMA standard medical receipt software. It accepts a patient number or patient name input, determines whether the input is a half-width numeric patient ID or a full-width Kana/Kanji name, and then searches the patient master database to resolve and return the corresponding patient ID and patient number. It handles group/branch hospital configurations and patient number construction management.
purpose.domain: healthcare / medical records (Japanese medical receipt system)

notable_features: Japanese-language comments encoded in latin-1 (actually EUC-JP or Shift-JIS, decoded as latin-1 producing mojibake)
COPY directives for multiple include files (CPPTINF.INC, CPPTNUM.INC, CPSYSKANRI.INC, CPSK1009.INC, MCPAREA, etc.)
CALL to external subprograms: ORCSKANACHK2, ORCSPTID, orcsstring, and DB access routines
LINKAGE SECTION with COPY-based parameter area (CPORCSPTNUM.INC, COMMON-SPA)
MCP (Message Control Program) style DB access pattern (MCP-TABLE, MCP-PATHNAME, PERFORM 910-DBSELECT-SEC)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — DB access is via CALL/PERFORM abstraction layer
DISPLAY statement left in code (debug trace: DISPLAY 'WRK-NAME:' WRK-NAME)

verdict.notes: The file is part of the well-known open-source ORCA (JMA standard receipt software) project from Japan. Japanese comments are garbled because the file is EUC-JP or Shift-JIS encoded but was decoded as latin-1. The COPY statements reference external copybooks not shown here. A DISPLAY debug statement remains in section 201-NAME-HEN-SEC, which is unusual for production but common in ORCA source releases. No COMP-3 usage despite numeric fields, which is consistent with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL usage on Linux. The 'copy_count: 0' in mechanical indicators likely means the COPY directives were not counted by the tool, but they are clearly present in the source.
